transcript: This might be the most chronically online theater piece I've ever seen. The Last Bimbo of the Apocalypse is a new musical inspired by a photo published in the New York Post in 2006 of Lindsay Lohan, Britney Spears, and Paris Hilton in a car together. There's an unidentified fourth girl from the scene who's out of frame, and in this musical, three internet personalities investigate who she is and what happened to her. Dripping with pop culture references and touting a techno-pop-rock score, this show is about artifice, celebrity culture, and Gen Z's internet in 2025. I thought it was great — it's a funny premise, the music is full of bops, and the singing is really good, with Keri René Fuller and Luke Islam as the vocal standouts. I probably fall into the target audience for this, as a young person who spends too much time online. I found the whole thing clever and entertaining, but I could see others finding it confusing or vacuous. But it's not meant to be taken seriously, and I'd argue that its pointlessness is kind of the point. With that, another program for my collection.
